agents.reason: Every kind the flight kind catalog states flies by this module; a kind names the module it uses and states a value for each parameter below that a kind supplies.

clock.reason: Shared real time: step n is the nth 100 ms since the Unix epoch, read from the server's clock, so every page showing a world shows its birds in the same places at the same moment, and one computation of an episode serves them all; the birds keep flying at normal speed while the people are paused or sped up. A world whose clock is coupled reads the same flight on its own timeline, so its birds stop when its people stop (docs/world-clock-contract.md). Nothing is stored: a flight is derived from a world version and its episode, with each flyer's choices drawn from the seed. When a model decides for a flyer, its choices must be recorded before viewers can share them.

output.reason: Per flyer and step: position in millimetres, velocity in millimetres a second, the signed turning acceleration, the state and whether it flaps. A renderer draws bank, pitch and flap from these and runs no steering of its own.

parameters.name: approach_height_mm
parameters.reason: How far above its perch a flyer turns from flying to a vertical landing, and where a take-off ends: at least one grid cell, so the column it descends is checked cell by cell, and at most 5 m.

parameters.name: body_span_mm
parameters.reason: A kind's wingspan. A perch bears a kind no wider than the span it declares, and the air is grown by half the widest kind's span around every part, so a flyer whose point keeps to free cells keeps its whole body out of every object. From a 5 cm insect to a 20 m winged creature, which the grown air leaves little room to fly in.

parameters.name: ceiling_mm
parameters.reason: The declared top of every flight volume above its ground: a saved world states no sky, so the module declares one. Twice the tallest kind the world object catalog places (the lamp post, 6,000 mm), so a flyer can pass over everything a person puts down.

parameters.name: cell_mm
parameters.reason: The side of an occupancy cell. Half a metre is coarse enough that a 24 m square by 12 m volume is 55,296 cells, and fine enough that a lamp post's 150 mm pole blocks one column of cells rather than a 2 m block.

parameters.name: climb_rate_mm_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind climbs while flying.

parameters.name: clock_reach_steps
parameters.reason: How far from the flight's clock, either way, a window may start: one episode. A page reads the minute ahead of the clock and never needs more than an episode behind it, so a window further off is refused by name (flight_step_out_of_range) and a server computes only the episodes around the clock.

parameters.name: containment_margin_mm
parameters.reason: How far inside the volume's sides and altitude band a flyer's predicted position must stay before containment steers it back: two cells, so steering turns a flyer well before the guard would have to stop it.

parameters.name: cruise_speed_mm_s
parameters.reason: The speed a kind flies at when nothing slows it.

parameters.name: descent_rate_mm_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind descends while flying.

parameters.name: episode_steps
parameters.reason: Five simulated minutes a flight episode. Every flyer starts an episode perching at its home perch and ends it there, so a request computes at most one episode from its start, whatever step it asks for.

parameters.name: flap_cycle_ms
parameters.reason: How long one wingbeat takes in the renderer; presentation only, never read by the step.

parameters.name: glide_speed_mm_s
parameters.reason: A kind flying level at or above this speed glides; below it, or climbing, it flaps.

parameters.name: homing_steps
parameters.reason: The last simulated minute of an episode, in which every flyer goes home and lands: at a small bird's cruise speed a minute crosses the volume's 34 m diagonal ten times over, so a flyer not home by the end is a finding, not a schedule.

parameters.name: landing_rate_mm_s
parameters.reason: How fast a kind descends its perch's column to land.

parameters.name: lookahead_ms
parameters.reason: How far ahead obstacle avoidance and containment look: one second of the flyer's own velocity.

parameters.name: max_accel_mm_s2
parameters.reason: The most steering can change a kind's velocity in a second.

parameters.name: max_altitude_mm
parameters.reason: The top of the band a kind flies in, above the ground and below the ceiling.

parameters.name: max_bank_mrad
parameters.reason: The steepest bank the renderer draws a kind at; presentation only.

parameters.name: max_cells
parameters.reason: The most cells a flight's grid may have: building the grid and searching a route home grow with it. 262,144 cells cover a 52 m square ground to the ceiling; a wider ground is refused by name (flight_world_too_large) rather than served slowly.

parameters.name: max_flyers
parameters.reason: The most flyers one world's volume holds: the largest number whose frame time was measured within one 60 Hz frame on a release build (docs/evaluation/2026-09-25-flight-bounds-v2.json). A world whose objects would host more is refused by name, never trimmed.

parameters.name: max_parts
parameters.reason: The most object parts a flight's air is built from: every part is placed and marked in the grid when a flight is composed. A world whose objects have more is refused by name (flight_world_too_large).

parameters.name: max_speed_mm_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind flies. At 100 ms steps a move then covers at most 2,000 mm, four cells, all of which the guard checks.

parameters.name: max_steps_per_request
parameters.reason: One simulated minute a request: a page asks for the next minute while it plays the current one.

parameters.name: max_turn_rate_mrad_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind turns, bounded as turning acceleration: never more than its speed times this rate.

parameters.name: min_altitude_mm
parameters.reason: The bottom of the band a kind flies in, above the ground; only landing and taking off go lower, inside a perch's own column.

parameters.name: perch_seconds_maximum
parameters.reason: The longest a kind stays on a perch before choosing again.

parameters.name: perch_seconds_minimum
parameters.reason: The shortest a kind stays on a perch before choosing again.

parameters.name: roam_seconds_maximum
parameters.reason: The longest a kind wanders before choosing a perch.

parameters.name: roam_seconds_minimum
parameters.reason: The shortest a kind wanders before choosing a perch.

parameters.name: roam_weight_milli
parameters.reason: Of a kind's choices when a perch ends, the share, in thousandths, that wander for a while before choosing a perch.

parameters.name: route_cells
parameters.reason: The most cells one search for a route home may settle before it ends with no route; the flyer then steers for its home's approach point, and one not home when its episode ends is named. Over twelve development seeds in the four measured worlds no search settled more than 119 cells. Unbounded, a search that finds no route on the largest grid the module admits settles every free cell of the band first; bounded, it ends after these (both timed in docs/evaluation/2026-09-26-flight-worker.json).

parameters.name: route_searches
parameters.reason: The most searches for a route home one flyer makes in an episode: the first when it turns home, then one each time the guard has held it for ten steps on its way. Over twelve development seeds in the four measured worlds no flyer searched more than twice in an episode. Unbounded, flyers the guard held again and again, steered straight at a crown, searched 32, 35 and 61 times in one homing minute, which tests/test_flight_search_bounds.py measures beside the bound it holds.

parameters.name: slowing_radius_mm
parameters.reason: Within this distance of where it is heading a flyer slows in proportion, so it arrives at its perch's approach point at rest.

parameters.name: takeoff_rate_mm_s
parameters.reason: How fast a kind climbs its perch's column to take off.

parameters.name: wander_distance_mm
parameters.reason: How far ahead of a wandering flyer the circle its wander target moves on is centred.

parameters.name: wander_jitter_mm
parameters.reason: How far a wander target may move on its circle in one step, drawn from the seed.

parameters.name: wander_radius_mm
parameters.reason: The radius of the circle a wander target moves on.

modules.reason: Flight over a world's own geometry: Reynolds steering (seek, arrive, wander, obstacle avoidance, containment) over an integer point mass, a coarse occupancy grid built from the placed objects' catalog parts, an altitude band inside the volume, and take-off, flying, landing and perching as states. A bird, a dragon and a plane are kinds of the flight kind catalog, never code.

space.reason: A saved world's ground area, read where its ground states one and declared where it states none, as the society declares its walking area, from the ground to the declared ceiling.

agents.reason: Every thing kind whose moves name this module (assets/catalogs/things/kinds) flies by it, and states a value for every parameter below that a kind supplies. A kind's figures are declared for the screen, not measured from an animal: a society minute plays in 8 s at 1x, so a large flyer's world speeds of 1 to 3 m/s show as 7.5 to 22.5 m/s.

clock.reason: One call is one simulated minute of the society's persisted history, as a walking tick is, and inside it the module takes steps_per_minute steps of step_ms each. Nothing of a flight is kept between minutes but the flyer's own state: its route is found again each minute from where it is.

output.reason: The flew event's payload: a waypoint [x, y, height] in millimetres at the end of each simulated second, the took_off and landed events with the millisecond of the minute each happened at, the goal's status or its refusal by name, how many steps the guard held, and the digest of the air it was flown in. A renderer draws the flyer along the waypoints and runs no steering of its own.

parameters.name: acceleration_mm_per_s2
parameters.reason: The most a kind's speed along its heading changes in a second; steering asks for a change and is held to this.

parameters.name: band_minimum_mm
parameters.reason: The lowest a kind cruises above the ground; where the columns ahead stand taller it flies higher, its clearance above their tops, up to the air's ceiling.

parameters.name: ceiling_mm
parameters.reason: The highest ceiling an air may state above its ground; an air states its own ceiling at or below it. Twice the highest band a kind may state, so every band fits under it with room to clear what stands below.

parameters.name: clearance_mm
parameters.reason: How far above the tops of the columns under its body a kind keeps, except over open ground while it lands or takes off: 1 m for a small bird to 20 m for a creature whose wings reach far beyond its body. A column whose top and this clearance reach above the air's ceiling is not flyable for the kind.

parameters.name: climb_mm_per_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind climbs.

parameters.name: column_maximum_mm
parameters.reason: The widest column an air may have. An air's column is half its widest flyer's span rounded up to 500 mm and held between the narrowest and the widest, so a column is about the reach of a wing and a street never becomes a single column.

parameters.name: column_minimum_mm
parameters.reason: The narrowest column an air may have: at 2 m, the most columns an air may have cover a 1,024 m square, and a route search over them stays bounded.

parameters.name: cruise_mm_per_s
parameters.reason: The speed a kind flies at when nothing slows it, declared for the screen: a society minute plays in 8 s at 1x, so 1 to 3 m/s in the world shows as 7.5 to 22.5 m/s for a large flyer.

parameters.name: descent_mm_per_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind descends, and the slope it glides down to land: its descent over its cruise speed.

parameters.name: hovers
parameters.reason: 1 for a kind that can hold still in the air, a floating spirit or a hovering bird: told to stay, it slows to rest where it is, and it rises and lands straight up and down. 0 for a winged kind, which stays by circling at its smallest turn and lands down a spiral where the ground around the point is open.

parameters.name: max_columns
parameters.reason: The most columns an air may have: reading an air and searching a route grow with it. 262,144 columns cover a 1,024 m square at the narrowest column and a 4,096 m square at the widest; a larger air is refused by name (flight_world_too_large) rather than flown slowly.

parameters.name: max_flyers
parameters.reason: The most flyers one world's minute moves, as flight v1 bounds its flyers: a world whose things would fly more is refused by name (too_many_flyers), never trimmed.

parameters.name: route_cells
parameters.reason: The most columns one route search may settle before it ends with no route, which refuses the goal as no_route: a sixteenth of the largest air, so a search that finds no way ends in bounded time.

parameters.name: span_mm
parameters.reason: A kind's wingspan, from its extent. Its body is the square of half its span around its position: the columns that square meets are the ones it must clear, and the ones a landing or a take-off needs open.

parameters.name: step_ms
parameters.reason: The length of one step, each steered, moved and held to the guard: a step at the fastest cruise moves 2.5 m, and the guard asks every column the box the move sweeps meets.

parameters.name: steps_per_minute
parameters.reason: Steps in one society minute: this many steps of step_ms make the minute the society persists.

parameters.name: turn_rate_mrad_per_s
parameters.reason: The fastest a kind turns: its heading turns at most this far in a second, so its smallest turn is its cruise speed over this rate, the radius it circles at when it stays.

parameters.name: waypoints_per_minute
parameters.reason: One waypoint at the end of each simulated second, every second step: a renderer moves the flyer between them.

modules.reason: Flight for beings: a flying thing moved one society minute at a time through a world's air columns by Reynolds steering with bounded acceleration and turning, at a height that clears the column tops ahead by its kind's clearance under the air's ceiling, every step held to a guard, by a route over flyable columns where the straight way is blocked, toward the goals a things engine gives it: go near, keep near, circle, land, take off and stay.

space.reason: A world's ground divided into square columns, row by row from its least corner, each holding the height of the tallest solid in it, 0 where it is open, under a ceiling. The module reads an air as it is given; composing one from a world's geometry is a host's work above this package.

agents.reason: The traffic simulation's vehicle classes (assets/catalogs/traffic/vehicle-class.v1.json), each bounded by that catalog's own integer fields and their cited sources.

clock.reason: Shared real time: second n is the nth second since the Unix epoch, read from the server's clock, as the flight's step n is its nth 100 ms, so every page showing a world shows its vehicles in the same places at the same moment, and one computation of an episode serves them all. Nothing is stored: traffic is derived from a world's road records and version, with every choice drawn from the seed. Under a legacy world clock the society's one-minute tick is not this clock and does not move it: vehicles keep driving at normal speed while the people are paused or sped up, and no crossing a walker makes is fed to traffic. A world whose clock is coupled moves this module on its own traffic timeline, after its society's minutes, and feeds it the crossings its walkers occupy (docs/world-clock-contract.md).

output.reason: The traffic presentation frame (exulanica.traffic-presentation-frame/v1) of every second of a window, grouped by vehicle: its axles, the path its front passed, its mode, speed and place each second, and its class, body family, colour and dimensions once. A renderer draws the body from these and moves it along the path, never across its corners. Version 2 adds each signal (exulanica.traffic-signal-presentation/v1): its groups, where their heads stand, and the indication each shows every second, the one the step obeyed.

parameters.name: clock_reach_steps
parameters.reason: How far from the clock, either way, a window may start: one episode. A page reads the minute ahead of the clock, so a window further off is refused by name (traffic_second_out_of_range) and a server computes only the episodes around the clock.

parameters.name: departure_steps
parameters.reason: The first 600 seconds of an episode, in which each vehicle leaves home once, at a second drawn from the seed; the rest of the episode is for its stay and its drive home. Measured on episode 0 of 48 generated towns whose traffic drives, 24 of each preset in assets/catalogs/world-recipes/world-recipe.v2.json (lane W5's departures sample and 40 more drawn the same way), once a vehicle with another standing between it and its stop line waits outside the junction: with 600 no town's traffic locked, every trip arrived and every vehicle was home by second 1008, and some vehicle moved in a median 565.5 of the 1,200 seconds of a small town and 845 of a market town (469 and 640.5 with 300); with 900, 22 towns still had vehicles away from home at the episode's end. Before that rule, 2 of these towns locked at 600.

parameters.name: dwell_steps_maximum
parameters.reason: The longest a vehicle stays where it drove to before it drives home, drawn from the seed.

parameters.name: dwell_steps_minimum
parameters.reason: The shortest a vehicle stays where it drove to before it drives home.

parameters.name: episode_steps
parameters.reason: Twenty minutes an episode. Every vehicle starts an episode parked at home, where the fleet's genesis places it, and a vehicle not parked at home at the episode's last second is named in the window, not moved.

parameters.name: fleet_share_permille
parameters.reason: The share, in thousandths, of each parking kind's places that hold a vehicle when an episode starts: half, so every vehicle has a place free to drive to and none takes another's home.

parameters.name: max_steps_per_request
parameters.reason: One minute a request: a page asks for the next minute while it plays the current one.

parameters.name: max_vehicles
parameters.reason: The most vehicles one world's traffic drives: a world whose home places would host more is refused by name (roads_world_too_large), never trimmed.

modules.reason: Road movement: the traffic simulation (exulanica/traffic) driving a world's road records second by second: cars, vans, buses and bicycles keep their lanes, stop at stop lines, take turns at junctions by the junction's rule and park. A host above this package (exulanica/world/traffic_host.py) composes a world's records and has a worker process compute whole episodes, deriving the lane connections and parking spaces the records imply; the step is advance_traffic, one simulated second a call.

space.reason: A compiled road network: a world's city road records with the lane connections and parking spaces traffic derives from them (exulanica/traffic/city_derivation.py): lanes, directional connections, conflict zones, crossings and parking.

agents.reason: The inhabitants of every society engine that routes its people over a graph. Version 1 keeps its frozen seeded motion, which has no routes, and is not moved by any module.

clock.reason: One tick is one simulated minute of the society's persisted history, advanced by a person's request or the host's playback.

output.reason: Every inhabitant's motion_path_mm: each segment traversed in the tick, start and end included, or one stationary point. A renderer interpolates along it, never across its corners.

parameters.name: budget_mm_per_tick
parameters.reason: The travel one tick may spend along a route: a society's recorded movement budget or a living inhabitant's walk speed. At most a thousand kilometres a tick, a guard on a stored figure far past any walk.

parameters.name: clearance_mm
parameters.reason: How far a walker's centre keeps from anything that blocks walking: the lattice is inset by it and a node or edge nearer an obstacle is removed.

parameters.name: new_society_budget_mm_per_tick
parameters.reason: The movement budget a new purposeful society records in its state: 60 m a one-minute tick, at most a metre each simulated second. A stored society walks at the budget its own state records, never this figure.

modules.reason: Walking over a graph of integer-millimetre nodes and edges: shortest routes by integer edge length with lexicographic node-path ties, and a budgeted traversal that interpolates each point with integer floor division.

space.reason: The route graph a society's input or a living society's place states: a district's sidewalk graph, a saved world's declared lattice, the walking surfaces a generated world's records state, or a living place's walking graph.
